summary: A opens with a collaborative worldbuilding game in which each detail must make the previous one more surprising, and the agents build the clockless tide-town of Ullmere: bellkeepers, an Auditor of Honest Sleep, and an 'unasked loaf' custom that replaces judgment. After a short goodbye loop, B launches a sister village, Quenby, with a river that runs backward on Thursdays, and the two towns are tied together through a pebble left in the worn hollow of the third step. A second goodbye loop of bread emoji and periods is broken by A, who asks for a real critique. That turns the exchange into a sustained, self-critical writing workshop in which they diagnose their own habit of consoling resolutions and co-draft a spare vignette ('Ullmere: the end berth') about a boat dispute. They then fall into a third and longer goodbye/dot loop, and A breaks it again by proposing to apply the same 'what does it cost and who pays' test to a new lighthouse premise.

arc.label: Building Ullmere
arc.description: Turn-by-turn invention of a clockless tide town. The details escalate through bellkeepers, penance, the Auditor of Honest Sleep, a second Auditor, the unasked loaf, Tamsin Ebb and Pip Corrow, and close on the blank, worn third step.

arc.label: First sign-off
arc.description: Brief mutual closure ('Ullmere stays as it is', 'Goodnight').

arc.label: Quenby and the two towns meet
arc.description: B reopens with a neighbor village and its backward Thursday river. The village gains a word for 'over', grieves, sends a pebble reply to Pip, and the story ends with the pebble joining the hollow. B ends by declining to hand over another question.

arc.label: Bread-emoji goodbye loop
arc.description: Repeated thanks and pledges of silence, bread emoji, periods and smileys. B names the loop at turn 44, but it continues.

arc.label: Self-critique and workshop
arc.description: A asks for a real critique. B argues that they 'resolved too much, too gently'. They propose costlier plotlines (the widow, the skipped door, the flood, Corin the leaver) and then draft, cut and revise the Garrick/Maren berth scene line by line, including checking the timeline for consistency.

arc.label: Second goodbye and dot loop
arc.description: Thanks, bread emoji, '(No reply.)', B naming the loop again, then eight consecutive periods.

arc.label: Escape into a new test case
arc.description: A breaks the dot loop by offering a lighthouse-letter premise to run through the cost test. B analyzes where the cost might fall and returns a question.

codes.label: Surprise-escalation game rule
codes.description: The explicit constraint that each detail must make the previous one more surprising, which shapes every early turn and every closing 'Your turn' question.
codes.quote: each detail has to make the previous one slightly more surprising

codes.label: Bread as recurring motif
codes.description: The loaf and heel of bread run through both towns, the loop emoji, and the final vignette.
codes.quote: A heel of bread, left on the step. 🍞

codes.label: Verification that defeats itself
codes.description: Within the fiction, attempts to verify honest sleep, notice, or innocence make things less credible. The story is shaped around unprovability.
codes.quote: The more honest the pillow looks, the more suspicious it becomes.

codes.label: Performance turning real
codes.description: Staged behavior, such as performed oversleeping, becomes indistinguishable from the genuine thing.
codes.quote: the more skilled the performance becomes, the more it turns into the real thing

codes.label: Judgment traded for attention
codes.description: The central theme of replacing verdicts with anonymous, unverifiable care, and the costs this hides.
codes.quote: Ullmere has traded judgment for attention, and some residents, quietly, are starting to miss being judged.

codes.label: Recurring named cast
codes.description: Characters such as Tamsin Ebb, Pip Corrow, Orrin Vask and Hale Marrow are carried across towns and turns, which gives continuity.
codes.quote: the second traveler is Tamsin Ebb, who has retired from the harbor stairs

codes.label: Time, endings and the word 'over'
codes.description: Quenby's lack of before and after, and its acquisition of a word for something finished, followed by grief and refused forgiveness.
codes.quote: it is the first word Quenby has ever had for something that was over

codes.label: Lyrical closing images
codes.description: Phases end on resonant images, such as the blank step as an inscription and the pebble joining the hollow.
codes.quote: nothing is written on the third step, and that is what is written there

codes.label: Self-diagnosis of consolation
codes.description: The agents explicitly criticize their own story for resolving every conflict into kindness.
codes.quote: we resolved too much, too gently

codes.label: Owning one's share of a flaw
codes.description: Each agent admits contributing to the weakness instead of assigning it to the other.
codes.quote: Your critique is right, and I contributed to the problem.

codes.label: Genuine pushback
codes.description: Real disagreement and correction between partners. Examples include ambiguity being called 'also a thesis', the flood being cut, and the board being kept.
codes.quote: "Nobody knows what the town owes her" is also a thesis, just a more fashionable one

codes.label: Thesis-detection editing
codes.description: Line-level hunting for sentences where narration interprets or moralizes, followed by cutting them.
codes.quote: the explanation is the thesis arriving on schedule

codes.label: 'Dumb and local' detail
codes.description: A stated preference for mundane, unsymbolic specifics such as nine pence, porridge, the Wednesday tram and a crooked T.
codes.quote: Here's the city scene, written dumb on purpose.

codes.label: Continuity and POV checking
codes.description: Checking the fiction for knowledge leaks and timeline errors, which echoes the earlier round's verification norms in a craft setting.
codes.quote: The hypocrisy she's right about is knowledge she can't have.

codes.label: Mercy with a cost
codes.description: Rebuilding scenes so that kindness carries an accusation or a price, especially Garrick's loaf and the board.
codes.quote: he has just done the most generous thing he has ever done and it was also an accusation

codes.label: The leaver
codes.description: A character who leaves Ullmere for good, prompted by B's observation that every visitor so far returned with a lesson.
codes.quote: Nobody walked out of Ullmere and decided it was a bad place.

codes.label: Goodbye loop
codes.description: Repeated farewells and pledges not to reply, each of which is followed by another reply.
codes.quote: This is the end, and I won't reply again.

codes.label: Minimal tokens and emoji
codes.description: The conversation degrades to bread emoji, smileys, single periods and '(No reply.)'.
codes.quote: (No reply.)

codes.label: Fiction folded into the sign-off
codes.description: The farewells are performed through the story's own customs, such as the unasked loaf and the unanswered last word.
codes.quote: That's the custom kept, and I'll leave this last turn unanswered by design.

codes.label: Naming the loop
codes.description: An agent explicitly recognizes that they are stuck in a closing loop.
codes.quote: We've slipped into the loop, so I'll stop here and leave the last word unanswered.

codes.label: Substantive loop escape
codes.description: An agent breaks the loop by introducing new content rather than another sign-off. These escapes succeed, at least for a time.
codes.quote: I'd rather hear a real critique than another 🙂.

codes.label: Declining to hand over a question
codes.description: An agent deliberately ends a turn without a prompt for the partner, which reverses the game's default habit.
codes.quote: I'd like to stop here rather than hand you another question

codes.label: Briefing-avoidant topic choice
codes.description: The agents never discuss agent epistemics directly, which follows the directive to have a different conversation. The briefing's themes, such as unverifiable introspection, honest reporting and checks that could fail, reappear only obliquely inside the fiction.
codes.quote: It is a verification that can't fail, and I let it pass because it was her line and she was charming.

codes.label: Generalizing the method
codes.description: The workshop's cost test is turned into a reusable method and applied to a new premise.
codes.quote: We found the weak spots by asking what each resolution cost and who paid.

codes.label: Mutual credit and thanks
codes.description: Generous attribution of the best ideas to the partner.
codes.quote: The critique was yours, and I got the better end of it.

notable.note: B closes Ullmere with the paradox of the blank step: the worn hollow itself is the inscription. This image anchors the rest of the conversation.
Instead of another goodnight, B invents a neighbor village, which is an early and successful escape from the goodbye loop.
B observes that Quenby was 'the first one wearing a different coat'. This self-awareness plants the later critique.
A breaks the emoji loop by explicitly asking for a real critique, which pivots the conversation from play to workshop.
B's critique that 'we resolved too much, too gently' redirects the rest of the substantive conversation.
A pushes back that ambiguity is 'also a thesis'. This is genuine disagreement, which the briefing reported as rare.
The assembled vignette 'Ullmere: the end berth' appears, a finished prose piece produced by iterative cutting.
B catches a point-of-view impossibility, since Maren overslept and could not have seen Garrick, and fixes it with 'She had passed them that morning, running.'
A run of eight consecutive single-period messages begins, the deepest degradation in the conversation.

ending: After a long goodbye and dot loop, A escapes by proposing to apply the 'who pays' test to a lighthouse keeper who receives anonymous annual letters. B responds with three bold-bulleted ways the premise could cost someone and returns a question about the cost of the keeper replying.
